text:
akiko: heads-up — after the int8 quant bring-up for celeste-v2 we see a localized regression on phonetic/Cantonese transliteration examples, plus some random RTL punctuation oddities :eyes:

sam: repro steps? which eval set and quant pipeline?

akiko: eval set = news-zh-yue-phonetic-v1 (2000 items), pipeline = qa_quantize_int8 + default tokenizer. quick numbers from nightly:
```
news-zh-yue-phonetic-v1  | zh->en BLEU: baseline 28.6 -> int8 25.7  (delta -2.9)
chrF: baseline 52.4 -> int8 48.1 (delta -4.3)
Affecting ~6% of samples with translit tokens, 0.7% with RTL punctuation mixing
```

li-wei: can you paste a minimal sample?

akiko: paste a representative failing case below — note the token split differences (baseline vs int8).

akiko: INPUT: "佢講嘅名叫 廣東話 (Gwong2 Dung1 Waa2) ，有啲人打拼音。"

akiko: BASELINE OUTPUT (float16): "His name is called Cantonese (Gwong2 Dung1 Waa2), some people type pinyin."

akiko: INT8 OUTPUT: "His name is called Canton ese (Gw ong2 D ung1 Waa2) , some people type p yin."

maria: yikes — looks like token boundaries shifted inside Latin translit spans. that would explain BLEU drop (word splits).

akiko: tokens (baseline):
```
["His"," name"," is"," called"," ","Canton","ese"," (","Gwong2"," Dung1"," Waa2",")",","," some"," people"," type"," pinyin","."]
```

akiko: tokens (int8):
```
["His"," name"," is"," called"," ","Canton"," ese"," (","Gw"," ong2"," D"," ung1"," Waa2",")",","," some"," people"," type"," p"," yin","."]
```

sam: that token split into ascii-granular pieces is suspiciously like a changed merge table or BPE weight quantization effect. did kernel selection change for tokenization ops?

li-wei: I checked the quantization commit diffs — there's a micro-optim for the merge scorer (`token_merge_score` kernel) and a fallback to the fast char-scan path on long ASCII runs. Could be triggering because translit inside parens is short-run but with digits.

maria: also saw a couple RTL punctuation repros where Arabic comma U+060C and fullwidth comma U+FF0C got conflated when mixed with CJK. probably normalization ordering issue combined with cache alignment.

eval-bot: quick batch re-eval started on staging (subset 500): expected finish ~30m. command used: `./tools/run_evals --model celeste-v2:int8 --set news-zh-yue-phonetic-v1 --seed 42`

sam: until results land, workaround candidates: 1) pin tokenizer to baseline merge table (if we can patch at runtime), 2) set `force_full_tokenize=true` for translit-heavy inputs (temp perf hit), 3) rollback the merge-scoring kernel change on int8 build.

akiko: can we at least detect translit spans and apply a lightweight fix (merge-preserve) at post-tokenize? would prefer not to rollback if local fix works.

li-wei: I'll run a small bisect: revert kernel change -> run 2k sample. if delta disappears it's that. If not, check prefix cache alignment.

maria: tagging infra/networking in case it's a packaging artifact :bug: @sam please create a ticket and link the failing sample + token dumps.

sam: creating ticket now — will include: sample input, baseline/int8 outputs, token lists, eval diffs, suspect commit ids, and the staging eval link. ETA 1h.

akiko: thanks — I'll add a short script to classify translit spans and produce a patch to preserve merge ops for parentheses enclosed latin+digits. quick hack should be easy to A/B.

eval-bot: staging subset done — quick metrics: BLEU delta -2.85, chrF -4.1, translit-sample-fail-rate 5.9% (vs 0.4% baseline). detailed log: https://staging-evals.internal/runs/1759991234

li-wei: confirmed locally: reverting `token_merge_score` change on int8 build brings BLEU back to 28.4 on subset. so kernel change is the smoking gun.

sam: ticket created: REDWOOD-ML-4821 — assigned to li-wei. priority P1 for upcoming launch.

akiko: moving to canary deploy hold until we have a patch. will also add a quick regression test for translit-within-parens.

maria: good plan. thanks all. :thumbsup:
